title: Low-Power and Superior Performance Design of Ternary Logic Cells Using CNFET and MOSFET Devices for VLSI Applications
problem: Ternary logic implementation faces challenges in power efficiency and performance
motivation: Ternary logic can provide efficiency benefits, but traditional MOSFET implementations have high power dissipation
method: The researchers design ternary logic cells (circuits using three operating states instead of the two used in standard transistors) using CNFETs (carbon nanotube transistors) and MOSFETs (standard silicon transistors), testing designs named NTI, PTI, and STI at 45nm technology. They exploit a key difference: CNFETs' threshold voltage—the electrical point where they turn on—can be tuned and adjusted, whereas MOSFETs cannot. This tunable property lets them optimize the ternary cells for both lower power consumption and superior performance.
key_novelty: Ternary logic cells built with carbon nanotube transistors (CNFETs) that have tunable threshold voltage achieve better power efficiency than those using standard silicon transistors (MOSFETs).
